chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaina, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays who said:

I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two greedy ones are never satiated — a seeker of the world and a seeker of knowledge. So whoever confines himself from the world to what God has made permissible for him is saved, and whoever takes it through other than its permissible means is destroyed, unless he repents or retracts. And whoever takes knowledge from its rightful people and acts according to his knowledge is saved, and whoever seeks the world by it — then it is his share.'

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: Its rightful people — in Shia tradition, refers specifically to the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt as the legitimate sources of religious knowledge
key_terms.حَظُّهُ: His portion/share — indicating that worldly-motivated knowledge yields only worldly reward, with no spiritual benefit
key_terms.مَنْهُومَانِ: Two insatiably greedy/gluttonous ones — the dual form emphasizes the parallel nature of the comparison

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about seekers of knowledge and seekers of the world?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), as reported by Imam Ali (AS) through the narrator Sulaym ibn Qays, draws a profound comparison between the insatiable desires of worldly seekers and knowledge seekers. While both types of seekers are equally driven, the hadith distinguishes between those who pursue the world within God's permitted limits (who are saved) versus those who seek it unlawfully (who are destroyed unless they repent). The decisive criterion for the knowledge seeker is whether their pursuit is for God's sake — taking knowledge from qualified sources and acting upon it — or merely for worldly gain, in which case worldly gain is all they will receive.
